Valuation date: 24-Jul-2026 | Output currency: USD | Accounting: IFRS | Primary method: FCFF DCF | Status: screen-grade / locally verified
Explicit FCFF DCF; debt-like bridge included

Base DCF indicates $8.71 per diluted share versus a frozen $1.73 market reference. The model is a screen-grade, formula-driven FCFF valuation; it assumes the low end of management’s 2026 revenue guidance is achieved and that cost savings and data-services mix raise normalized margins after 2026. The large gap to the market should be read as an execution / leverage / search-risk question—not as a standalone recommendation.

Catalysts: Q2 2026 delivery, evidence of restructure savings, data-services growth, and organic-search stabilization.

Risks: SEO / AI-search disruption, UK and Finland regulation, high leverage / deferred consideration, potential dilution, and integration / restructuring execution.

Evidence status: audited FY2023–FY2025, unaudited Q1 2026, management guidance, and a dated secondary market close. No licensed consensus or independently normalized peer data was used.

• Data-services growth and enterprise mix must offset Google-search disruption and UK / Finland regulatory headwinds.
• The AI transformation-led restructure must deliver a meaningful portion of its stated $13m annualized savings without damaging revenue.
• Borrowings, deferred consideration and capitalized-development spending must not absorb the forecast FCFF.
• 2026 guidance implies a second-half margin recovery after Q1’s 22% adjusted-EBITDA margin.

values: Traffic diversification, AI restructure savings, and data-services growth must offset poor organic search dynamics and UK / Finland regulation.
Data subscription mix must scale without returning to the 2026 Q1 cost base.
Working-capital and capitalized development needs must stay proportionate to revenue.

Management’s 2026 revenue and adjusted-EBITDA guidance is used as the starting point, but the model’s normalized EBITDA margin is an analyst estimate because the company’s adjusted measure excludes several items. The DCF uses FCFF, not management free cash flow, and treats capitalized development as capex.
Reverse DCF: implied 2031 normalized EBITDA margin at current price

The FCFF DCF is the primary method because Grandstand has a forecastable operating business and leverage is separately bridged. Deferred consideration and leases are explicitly deducted as debt-like claims. The reverse section reports model-derived implied expectations; it does not identify a unique market belief.

The company’s economics combine performance marketing, consumer and enterprise sports data, advertising, and ticketing. Available public comparables do not support a clean normalized peer median without licensed market data and manual financial normalization. The selected 4.0x–6.0x EBITDA range is therefore an analyst stress only. It is intentionally not averaged with the DCF.
